plan.title: release: Step 5 fast-before-slow gates + SHA suite stamp

narratives.Description: When shared task check co-lists cheap gates with the long vitest+coverage suite, late or early cheap failures still pay full suite cost if ordering is wrong. This story reorders gate-lists/orchestrator so fast preflight gates run before the expensive suite path for framework and consumer deposits. Release-local suite stamp remains owned by #3187; this story owns check composition ordering only.
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

Sibling to #3187 (auto-hatch branch coverage hairline without re-running the suite).

When `task release` Step 5 fails for a **small, non-suite** reason (e.g. `verify:cache-fresh` stale-by-drift after vitest already ran ~20–30m), the operator fixes the small issue and re-invokes release — which **re-runs the full check + vitest coverage suite** from scratch. There is no SHA-bound stamp and no “cheap gates first” split, so late/small failures cost a full suite.

**v0.97.0 evidence:** full Step 5 → coverage hairline → re-run with hatch → suite green, then fail on cache-fresh → fetch-all → **third** full Step 5.

## Goals

1. **Gate ordering:** run cheap/fast gates before the expensive vitest+coverage suite so cache/lifecycle noise fails in seconds, not after half an hour.
2. **Resume / stamp:** if suite already passed (or hatch-passed) at HEAD `S`, skip re-running the suite when only later gates or re-entry need work — fail closed if SHA/tree changed.

## Proposed design

### A. Split Step 5 (or underlying `task check` path used by release)

```
Step 5a — fast preflight (seconds–few min)
  cache-fresh, orphan-active, contained-writes --enforce, license-sync,
  contract-drift, branch policy surfaces, other non-vitest gates…

Step 5b — suite + coverage (long)
  vitest with coverage / thresholds (or #3187 auto-hatch path)
```

Release (and optionally `task check` composition) runs **5a → 5b**. Failures in 5a never pay for 5b.

### B. SHA-bound suite stamp (after green 5b or PASS_WITH_DEBT)

Write something like:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "headSha": "<git rev-parse HEAD>",
  "suite": "pass" | "pass_with_debt",
  "debtIssue": null | 3185,
  "recordedAt": "ISO-8601"
}
```

On re-entry at same clean HEAD: skip 5b, re-run 5a only (or only the failed gate).  
**Fail closed** if: dirty tree, HEAD ≠ stamp, stamp missing/corrupt, or suite config material change (optional later).

### C. Interaction with #3187

- #3187: one suite run → auto-hatch if ledger allows → continue **without** second suite.
- This issue: even without hatch, **don’t re-run suite** for late small failures or re-entry at same SHA.
- Together: typical cut pays **one** suite; cache-fresh fixes pay **fast only**.

## Non-goals

- Skip suite when HEAD moved or product sources changed.
- `vitest --changed` as release bar (must measure whole tree).
- Soft-pass real test failures.
- Rely on wall-clock or “last run was recent” without SHA binding.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Fast gates run before vitest+coverage on the release Step 5 path (and documented).
- [ ] Intentional fail of a fast gate (e.g. forced stale cache) fails without starting full coverage suite (observable in logs / timing).
- [ ] After suite green at SHA S, re-invoke release at same S after fixing only a fast-gate issue does **not** re-run vitest+coverage (stamp hit logged).
- [ ] Dirty tree or different HEAD invalidates stamp (suite runs again).
- [ ] Unit tests for stamp read/write/invalidation and ordering contract.
- [ ] `docs/RELEASING.md` + release skill updated.

## Consumer impact

| Surface | Helps consumers? |
|---|---|
| **Release-only stamp / Step 5 resume** | **No direct** — consumers do not run `task release` on the framework cut path. |
| **Fast-before-slow ordering in shared `task check` / gate lists** | **Yes, if** ordering lands in the shared check composition used by framework **and** consumer deposits — fail-fast on cheap gates (cache-fresh, branch, orphan, etc.) without waiting on long suites where those gates are co-listed. |
| **#3187 auto-hatch** | **No direct** — hatch is release Step 5 coverage-debt; consumers may have their own coverage thresholds but not this hatch ledger. |
| **Faster framework releases** | **Indirect yes** — more frequent/reliable `@deftai/directive` cuts, less operator burnout on release day. |
| **Pre-cut hygiene docs** | **Mild yes** if documented as optional consumer `task check` hygiene (cache-fresh before long local CI). |

**Recommendation in implementation:** put **ordering** in shared gate composition where safe (consumer benefit); keep **suite stamp / resume** release-scoped (or behind `task release` only) unless a separate consumer “check resume” story is filed.

## References

- #3187 — auto-hatch branch hairline (no fail+re-run for debt)
- #2866 — open-issue ledger hatch rules
- #3185 — v0.97.0 coverage-debt hatch
- #2859 — file-and-merge for real product defects
- Session: v0.97.0 cut (dirty tree → coverage fail → hatch re-run → cache-fresh fail → third full Step 5)

## Out of scope / later

- Coverage-only re-eval from saved `coverage-summary.json` without re-instrumenting (P3).
- Win32 worker / vitest 4 upgrade performance (#2634 class).

---

## Issue comment thread

_The issue body is the original write-up; maintainer comments below may supersede it. Read the full thread before building a dispatch envelope (#2143)._

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-07T15:21:27Z)

## Amendment (coordination with #3189 / #3187)

**Split ship paths:**
1. **Fast-before-slow ordering** — may land in **shared** `task check` / gate composition (helps consumers immediately; no #3189 required).
2. **SHA suite stamp / resume** — release-scoped v1 is fine; **general local check resume for consumers** should respect `plan.policy.checkResume` from **#3189** (default off when unset; CI never trusts local stamps).

**Related:**
- #3187 — auto-hatch (one suite for hairline); stamp should record `pass_with_debt` + issue number
- #3189 — policy + session nudge (consent for consumer resume/hatch expansion)

**Acceptance add:**
- [ ] Stamp never honored by CI required checks in v1.
- [ ] If `checkResume` policy exists and is `localStamp=off` or unset, consumer local check does not skip suite via stamp (release Step 5 may still use release-local stamp until unified).
narratives.UserStory: As a developer running task check, I want cheap gates to fail before the long coverage suite starts, so that cache and lifecycle noise costs seconds instead of half an hour.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1. In packages/core/src/check/gate-lists.ts order cheap gates (cache-fresh, orphan-active, branch policy, contract-drift class) before vitest/coverage suite entries. 2. In packages/core/src/check/orchestrator.ts (and cached-orchestrator if needed) ensure a fast-gate failure aborts before starting the coverage suite; log/timing evidence. 3. Unit tests in gate-lists.test.ts and orchestrator.test.ts prove ordering and fail-fast. 4. Brief CHANGELOG + any consumer-check docs cross-link. Do NOT edit packages/core/src/release/* or release skill (owned by #3187). Verify: npm test -w @deftai/directive-core -- --run check/gate-lists and check/orchestrator.

narrative.Acceptance: Given gate-lists used by task check / release check path, when listed, then non-vitest cheap gates appear before vitest+coverage suite entries.

items.title: Fast fail does not start suite

narrative.Acceptance: Given an intentional fast-gate failure, when orchestrator runs, then vitest+coverage suite does not start (observable in logs or test doubles).
Given check unit tests, when run, then ordering and fail-fast contracts are covered without live network.
Given merge, when CHANGELOG is read, then #3188 documents fast-before-slow check ordering.
